answer: Each account that wants to place an order must lock a stake in a shared contract, and the contract releases it only after the account completes a randomly assigned task verified by independent agents. Duplicate identities do not help: each must lock its own funds, while failed or abandoned tasks slash the stake. The meadow market can use an anchor stake sized to the order, so an attacker creating a hundred onyx identities must tie up capital a hundred times over and risks losing it.
